done_when: forge sync merges permissions.allow entries for Bash, Edit, Write, WebFetch and WebSearch into .claude/settings.json, keeping every entry and setting the client already has, and a second sync changes nothing. The destructive-command deny hook stays and still blocks first. A command-level test syncs a settings file with the client's own allow and deny entries and checks the result.
why: Claude Code sessions in client repos ask permission for every command because forge sync writes only hooks into .claude/settings.json, while Forge gives agents full access; Claude ignores a repo-level bypass mode, so the repo has to pre-allow the tools
